title: Woody Sez really cementing a timeline bio jukebox musical is a bit st...
transcript: Before Bob Dylan, there was Woody Guthrie, the grandfather of folk music in America who joined the labor unions and fought for people's rights through his music. And Woody says is his story on stage. Woody says both recounts his entire life as well as brings to life some of his famous folk hits, including, of course, This Land Is Your Land. And Woody Guthrie's life is so incredibly fascinating. I just wish that the show overall captured that spirit in a way that didn't feel like I was reading a Wikipedia entry. Unfortunately, because of the way that the narrative was set up here, it just felt like I was reading a chronological timeline of his life rather than really capturing the spirit of what he brought to America. He's such an interesting historical figure and parts of this made me want to know more about his life, just maybe not in this format. That being said, the performers who are actor musicians are incredible on that stage and I love getting to watch them perform these songs. I just wish the narrative kept me a little more locked in throughout what he says is playing at the Underbelly Bristol Square venue through the rest of the fringe.
